title: After the Rochester Tornado, a Sister Asked a Doctor for a Hospital
conflicts: Deaths: NWS gives 37 killed along the tornado's path; Clapesattle records about a score buried in Rochester in one day plus three or four later; used the NWS figure, labelled as the whole path. Beds: modern accounts say 27, 1889 newspapers quoted by Clapesattle say 45 (and Sister Joseph said they exaggerated); no bed count given. Mother Alfred's birth year 1828 vs 1829; no age given. St. Anthony Messenger's '$20,000 under projected cost' is unexplained and not used.
notes: Credits Mother Alfred Moes and the Sisters of St Francis with proposing and funding Saint Marys, and Dr W. W. Mayo with taking medical charge, following Clapesattle (1941) and Mayo's own 1894 and 1904 statements. Clapesattle cited from the Internet Archive scan. approx_date set to 1883-08 (the decision); the hospital opened 30 September 1889. Repeat screen flagged two other hospital editions as 'same-founder' (word overlap) but passed.
